sources.citation: Vandame, Charles. 1975. Notes sur l'organisation sociale, l'histoire, la vie rituelle, à Sara, village Kenga (Hadjeraï du Tchad). Journal de la Société des Africanistes 45(1): 69-114. DOI 10.3406/jafr.1975.1764.
sources.note: Ethnography read on Persée (PDF download could not be reached by automated download). Only linguistic remark is fn. 1 p. 69: 'les mots kenga ont été transcrits sans noter les tons ni les longueurs vocaliques'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2020. Central Sudanic Languages. Author manuscript (chapter for an OUP handbook of African languages), 13 pp. HAL halshs-03097024.
sources.note: Family-level overview: 'tone systems that may include up to four contrastive levels'; a typological table lists Kenga (possessive suffixes, SVO, noun-genitive). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Jacob, Peggy. 2017. Information structure in Sara-Bagirmi: A comparative approach to the synchronic state and diachronic development in the expression of information structure, with special attention to predicate-centered focus types. PhD dissertation, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, 197 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on word stress in Kenga (the words 'stress'/'accent' occur only for German/English examples). p. 22: the six languages studied, Kenga included, are 'tone languages with three level tones' (H/M/L), and fn. 6 notes that the Kenga literature marks all three tones; Kenga data drawn from Neukom 2010, Palayer 2004, Vandame 1968.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2009. Entre lac Albert et lac Tchad : l'expansion sara-bongo-baguirmienne. In Migrations et mobilité dans le bassin du Tchad (Maroua colloquium), 13 pp. HAL halshs-00348136.
sources.note: Comparative/historical; defines tones as pitch contrasts in SBB and gives Kenga cognates. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal & Pierre Nougayrol. 2008. Les langues soudaniques centrales : essai d'évaluation. Sprache und Geschichte in Afrika (SUGIA), 17 pp. HAL halshs-00348133.
sources.note: SBB languages have two-, three- or four-level tone systems; *SBB had two tones, western languages (Kenga among them, under *OCC > *SARA) added a third; Kenga appears in comparative lexical rows. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2006. Présentation des langues Sara-Bongo-Baguirmiennes. In P. Boyeldieu, P. Nougayrol & P. Palayer, Lexique comparatif historique des langues Sara-Bongo-Baguirmiennes (document électronique), 24 pp. Paris: CNRS-LLACAN.
sources.note: Comparative phonology of the SBB group (consonant, vowel and tone correspondence formulae). Kenga (source: Palayer 2004, Vandame 1968) is a 'western'/*OCC language with a three-register tone system; p. 9 notes Kenga has developed a vowel-length opposition in the initial syllable (CVCV/CV:CV). No mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2023. Tone split and tone replacement: diachronic pathways to a third tone level in 'western' SBB languages (Central Africa).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Recent account of the three-level tone systems of western SBB languages (Kenga belongs to this set); may summarise Kenga's tone inventory with references.
